findings.evidence: <select id="dob-day-select" autocomplete="bday-day" required=""> <select id="dob-month-select" autocomplete="bday-month" required=""> <select id="dob-year-select" autocomplete="bday-year" required="">
findings.fix: Use three short text fields for day, month and year, with the numeric input mode.
findings.violation: A date the person knows by heart is picked from three drop-downs, the year from 60 options.

findings.evidence: <label id="legalname-label" for="legalname-input">Your name</label> <input id="legalname-input" name="legal_name" type="text" required>, after <label id="name-label" for="name-input">Full name</label> <input id="name-input" name="full_name" required> earlier in the same form (line 11)
findings.fix: Remove the second name field, or if a legal name can differ from a preferred name, label both fields to say so and explain why the form needs both.
findings.violation: The form asks for the person's name twice, as 'Full name' and again as 'Your name', so the person must either repeat what they already typed or guess why a second name field exists.

findings.evidence: <input id="postal-input" name="postal_code" type="text" autocomplete="postal-code" required="" size="3"> (size=3)
findings.fix: Size the field to show at least 5 characters.
findings.violation: This postal code field shows 3 characters, too few to show a typical value whole while it is typed and checked.

findings.fix: Loosen the pattern to accept every valid way of writing the value, and normalise it after submission.
findings.violation: The pattern on this phone field rejects valid values such as +44 20 7946 0958; 020 7946 0958.

findings.evidence: <button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button>, placed after the 'Preferred contact time' field (line 71) and before the required Date of birth fieldset (lines 74 to 188); the primary submit carries no style at all: <button id="submit-btn" type="submit">Create account</button>
findings.fix: Style the primary submit (#submit-btn) as the most prominent control on the form, style 'View details' less prominently than it, and move any non-submit action so it never sits ahead of fields still to be filled in.
findings.violation: This secondary action is styled more prominently, with padding and a set font size, than the entirely unstyled primary submit button, and it sits before the form's last required fields (date of birth), so a person reaching it may read it as where to continue or finish rather than as subordinate to the plainer button three fields later.

findings.evidence: <label id="acctnum-label" for="acctnum-input">Account number</label> <input id="acctnum-input" name="account_number" type="text" inputmode="numeric" required>, two fields after <label id="member-label" for="member-input">Membership number (8 digits)</label> (line 40)
findings.fix: Remove the account-number field, or if it serves a real purpose, such as linking an existing loyalty account, make it optional and say in the label what number it expects and why.
findings.violation: This is a sign-up form creating a new account, so no account number can yet exist to enter, and the form already collected an identifying number as 'Membership number' a few fields earlier; requiring a second, differently named identifying number the task cannot use forces the person to guess what to type or abandon the field.

findings.evidence: <label id="contacttime-label" for="contacttime-input" style="display:inline-block;float:left;width:140px">Preferred contact time</label> <input id="contacttime-input" name="contact_time" type="text" required>
findings.fix: Drop this field from account creation and ask it only at the point a contact is actually being scheduled, such as during a support request.
findings.violation: Creating an account does not need to know when to call the person; a preferred contact time matters only once there is a reason to make contact, so requiring it here forces an answer the task cannot yet use.

findings.evidence: <fieldset id="row-dob"><legend>Date of birth</legend> ... three required selects for day, month and year (lines 74 to 188)
findings.fix: Remove the date-of-birth requirement unless an age limit applies, and if one does, say so next to the field and ask for only what the limit needs, such as a yes/no confirmation of being over the required age.
findings.violation: Nothing on the form states why creating an account needs a date of birth, so the task named by the heading and submit button cannot be shown to use this answer, and three required drop-downs must still be completed to satisfy it.

findings.evidence: font-size: 13px declared by its inline style
findings.fix: Set the field's font size to at least 16 pixels.
findings.violation: The text in this field is 13 pixels, below the 16 pixels at which a phone stops zooming the page on focus.
